title: Unexplained Income: Tax Rules & Changes Under IT Act, 2025
description: Unexplained income refers to any money, investment, or expenditure that a taxpayer cannot adequately account for or justify to the Income Tax Department. Hist.

faq.a: Unexplained income refers to any money, investment, or expenditure for which a taxpayer cannot provide a satisfactory explanation regarding its source or nature to the Income Tax Department. This includes cash credits, undisclosed investments, or unaccounted expenditures.

faq.q: Can I claim deductions against unexplained income?
faq.a: No, under both the previous regime and the Income Tax Act, 2025, no deductions, allowances, or set-off of losses are permitted against income categorised as unexplained. The entire amount is subject to the prescribed tax rate.

faq.q: What is the primary change introduced by the Income Tax Act, 2025, regarding unexplained income?
faq.a: The primary change is the introduction of a clear distinction in tax treatment and penalties based on whether the unexplained income is voluntarily disclosed by the taxpayer or detected by the Income Tax Department during an assessment or investigation.

faq.q: Is the basic exemption limit applicable to unexplained income?
faq.a: No, the basic exemption limit that applies to regular taxable income is not applicable to unexplained income. The entire amount of unexplained income is taxed at the specific rates prescribed for such income.

faq.q: What are the consequences of not disclosing unexplained income if detected by the department?
faq.a: If unexplained income is detected by the department, it attracts very high tax rates (potentially 75% or more, including surcharge) and significant penalties, which can range from 100% to 300% of the tax payable, leading to a substantial financial burden.

faq.q: Does the new Act make it easier to declare black money?
faq.a: The new Act aims to encourage *voluntary compliance* by offering a comparatively less punitive framework for self-disclosure. It does not make it "easier" to declare black money but rather provides an incentive for taxpayers to come clean before detection, thereby reducing litigation and increasing tax transparency.
